items.title: UK Property Market Data API - Prices, Rents, Yields, EPC
items.name: uk-property-market-data-api
items.description: Read UK property data by postcode, coordinates, what3words or town: asking and sold prices, rents, yields, growth and demand, planning applications, listed buildings, flood risk, EPC ratings, UPRNs, title ownership and leases, sale and rental valuations, and investment sourcing lists.

market-record.eventDescription: Charged once for each local area reading: asking prices, sold prices, long let and HMO rents, rental yields, capital growth, sales and rental demand, price per square foot, estate agent market share, build and rebuild costs, flood risk, conservation area and green belt checks, crime, demographics, income, population, council tax, internet speed and property stock by type or tenure. One row is a complete answer about one area. Locations the provider holds no data for are not charged.

property-record.eventDescription: Charged once for each single property answer: a property by its UPRN with its address parts, coordinates, use class and registered leases with their remaining years, a title number matched to a UPRN, a title with its address, type, ownership and lease information, an address matched to its UPRN, and sale, rental, HMO and historical valuations with the provider's estimate, margin and confidence. Priced above an area reading because one row is about one property rather than a neighbourhood.

list-record.eventDescription: Charged once for each record in a list answer: one planning application, one listed building, one freehold title, one UPRN, one EPC rating, one known floor area, one HMO register entry, one nearby school or one sourced investment property. Priced well below an area reading because a single request commonly returns dozens of these. Requests the provider returns nothing for are not charged.

account-record.eventDescription: Charged once for reading your own provider account: credits used and credits remaining on your plan. This is free at the provider and costs no credits there, so it is priced near zero here: checking what you have left before spending it should not itself cost anything worth counting.
